assertions.description: The WebTransport constructor exists (the reliability attributes extend it, so every other assertion builds on this).
reliability is a readonly attribute: an accessor with a getter and no setter on the prototype.
assertions.test: (() => { if (typeof WebTransport !== 'function') return false; const d = Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(WebTransport.prototype, 'reliability'); return !!d && typeof d.get === 'function' && d.set === undefined; })()

assertions.description: A newly constructed (still connecting) WebTransport reports reliability === "pending", per the constructor's [[Reliability]] = "pending" step.
assertions.test: (() => { if (typeof WebTransport !== 'function' || !('reliability' in WebTransport.prototype)) return false; try { const t = new WebTransport('https://127.0.0.1:44443/never'); t.ready.catch(() => {}); t.closed.catch(() => {}); const v = t.reliability; try { t.close(); } catch {} return v === 'pending'; } catch { return false; } })()

assertions.description: The value read from a live object is one of the WebTransportReliabilityMode enum strings: "pending", "reliable-only", or "supports-unreliable".
assertions.test: (() => { if (typeof WebTransport !== 'function' || !('reliability' in WebTransport.prototype)) return false; try { const t = new WebTransport('https://127.0.0.1:44443/never'); t.ready.catch(() => {}); t.closed.catch(() => {}); const v = t.reliability; try { t.close(); } catch {} return ['pending', 'reliable-only', 'supports-unreliable'].includes(v); } catch { return false; } })()

assertions.description: supportsReliableOnly is an own property of the WebTransport constructor (a static attribute) and reads as a boolean.
Being static, supportsReliableOnly is not on the prototype, so instances read undefined for it.
assertions.test: (() => { if (typeof WebTransport !== 'function' || !Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(WebTransport, 'supportsReliableOnly')) return false; if ('supportsReliableOnly' in WebTransport.prototype) return false; try { const t = new WebTransport('https://127.0.0.1:44443/never'); t.ready.catch(() => {}); t.closed.catch(() => {}); const v = t.supportsReliableOnly; try { t.close(); } catch {} return v === undefined; } catch { return false; } })()

assertions.description: Assigning to reliability on an instance in strict mode throws a TypeError, because the accessor has no setter.
assertions.test: (() => { 'use strict'; if (typeof WebTransport !== 'function' || !('reliability' in WebTransport.prototype)) return false; try { const t = new WebTransport('https://127.0.0.1:44443/never'); t.ready.catch(() => {}); t.closed.catch(() => {}); let threw = false; try { t.reliability = 'supports-unreliable'; } catch (e) { threw = e instanceof TypeError; } try { t.close(); } catch {} return threw; } catch { return false; } })()

assertions.description: After a session establishes, reliability becomes "supports-unreliable" (HTTP/3) or "reliable-only" (HTTP/2). Establishing a session needs a reachable HTTP/3 WebTransport endpoint, which this static showcase cannot provide.
assertions.test: Requires a live HTTP/3 WebTransport server; no such endpoint is reachable from this showcase, so the transition from "pending" cannot be executed here.
